paper_title: Dithiene-fused quinoxalineimide-based all-acceptor polymers for n-type organic semiconductors

qa_pairs.question: What are the structural components of the dithiene-fused quinoxalineimide (DTQI) building block, and how do its electronic properties compare to bithiophene imide (BTI)?
qa_pairs.answer: The DTQI building block combines the structural features of bithiophene imide (BTI) and quinoxaline (Qx). According to DFT calculations, DTQI possesses a completely planar structure and a calculated LUMO level of -2.60 eV, which is 0.3 eV lower than that of the BTI building block, indicating a stronger electron-deficient nature.
qa_pairs.source_title: Dithiene-fused quinoxalineimide-based all-acceptor polymers for n-type organic semiconductors

qa_pairs.question: Which catalyst system and coupling reaction are employed to synthesize the all-acceptor polymers PDTQI and P(DTQI-BTI)?
qa_pairs.answer: PDTQI and P(DTQI-BTI) are synthesized via Stille coupling polymerization using a Pd2(dba)3/P(o-tol)3 catalyst system.
qa_pairs.source_title: Dithiene-fused quinoxalineimide-based all-acceptor polymers for n-type organic semiconductors

qa_pairs.question: Compare the charge transport behavior and electron mobility of the homopolymer PDTQI with the copolymer P(DTQI-BTI).
qa_pairs.answer: PDTQI exhibits ambipolar charge transport with a hole mobility (μh) of 0.005 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ and an electron mobility (μe) of 0.012 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹. In contrast, P(DTQI-BTI) shows unipolar n-type transport with a significantly higher electron mobility of 0.25 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹.
qa_pairs.source_title: Dithiene-fused quinoxalineimide-based all-acceptor polymers for n-type organic semiconductors

qa_pairs.question: How does the incorporation of the dithiene-fused quinoxalineimide (DTQI) unit affect the LUMO levels and charge carrier injection in these polymers?
qa_pairs.answer: The DTQI unit, due to the strong electron-withdrawing imide and quinoxaline groups, results in deep-lying LUMO energy levels (below -3.50 eV). This deep LUMO level is beneficial for organic thin-film transistors as it facilitates electron injection and helps suppress the accumulation of holes.
qa_pairs.source_title: Dithiene-fused quinoxalineimide-based all-acceptor polymers for n-type organic semiconductors

qa_pairs.question: What evidence from thin-film characterization suggests that P(DTQI-BTI) has superior crystallinity compared to PDTQI?
qa_pairs.answer: P(DTQI-BTI) thin films show a higher root-mean-square (RMS) roughness of 0.515 nm compared to 0.408 nm for PDTQI. This higher roughness, combined with stronger molecular aggregation, indicates that P(DTQI-BTI) achieves higher crystallinity, which contributes to its improved electron mobility.
qa_pairs.source_title: Dithiene-fused quinoxalineimide-based all-acceptor polymers for n-type organic semiconductors

qa_pairs.question: What is the specific device architecture and dielectric material used to evaluate the DTQI-based polymers in organic thin-film transistors?
qa_pairs.answer: The devices utilize a top-gate/bottom-contact (TGBC) structure with Ag gate electrodes and polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) as the dielectric layer.
qa_pairs.source_title: Dithiene-fused quinoxalineimide-based all-acceptor polymers for n-type organic semiconductors

qa_pairs.question: What are the optimal solution-processing and thermal treatment conditions for achieving high performance in DTQI-based polymer transistors?
qa_pairs.answer: Optimal performance is achieved by processing the polymers from a chloroform solution at a concentration of 5 mg/mL, followed by a thermal annealing step at 100 °C for 20 minutes to optimize film morphology.
qa_pairs.source_title: Dithiene-fused quinoxalineimide-based all-acceptor polymers for n-type organic semiconductors

qa_pairs.question: What is the thermal decomposition temperature (5% weight loss) for the polymers PDTQI and P(DTQI-BTI)?
qa_pairs.answer: Both PDTQI and P(DTQI-BTI) exhibit high thermal stability with decomposition temperatures exceeding 400 °C.
qa_pairs.source_title: Dithiene-fused quinoxalineimide-based all-acceptor polymers for n-type organic semiconductors
